races.name: Tattersalls Ireland May Hit & P2P Sale Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Papillondelumiere
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits the likely pace scenario but badly outclassed on hurdles debut and 48 days off suggests rustiness.
runners_data.comment: Maiden pointer who was soundly beaten when 100-1 for last month's hurdle debut
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden pointer who was soundly beaten when 100-1 for last month's hurdle debut at Southwell (2m, good).

runners_data.name: Edelak
runners_data.note: Front-running style with decent Flat form but breathing issues reported last time and will need to settle better than usual.
runners_data.comment: Beaten at skinny odds when second this month but has strong claims again here
runners_data.spotlight: 1m4f Flat winner in Ireland last summer (useful form); only sixth of seven in Listed juvenile hurdle on stable debut in December (breathing issue reported) and found one too good when 2-7 favourite at Market Rasen (2m, good; first-time cheekpieces) this month; however, he was well clear of the others on that recent outing and looks the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Crackalackin
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with fair recent third at Fakenham but Luke Scott's 3lb claim helpful in tight finish.
runners_data.comment: Fair on the Flat; ran okay on hurdling debut; may have found Hexham too stiff last time
runners_data.spotlight: Fair Flat racer who won over 1m4f on Polytrack last autumn; began hurdling career with respectable third of four at Fakenham (2m, good) last month and didn't run badly before weakening into fourth at Hexham more recently; holds each-way claims at least here.

runners_data.name: Garde My Guinness
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 256-day absence which is a major concern despite consistent placed efforts previously.

runners_data.name: Backer Bilk
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse perfectly suited to likely pace with recent Hereford second showing readiness despite moderate opposition.
runners_data.comment: Did not achieve huge amount when well-held second at Hereford but has place claims again
runners_data.spotlight: Low-grade AW winner; did not achieve huge amount when well-held second of seven behind short-odds favourite at Hereford (2m, good) a fortnight ago, his second hurdle run, but might collect another minor prize here.

runners_data.name: Versatile
runners_data.note: Hold-up style ideal for race shape but 30 days off the Flat and regressive recent form raises questions.
runners_data.comment: Made fairly encouraging hurdle debut last month but has since refused to race on the Flat
runners_data.spotlight: Has regressed on the Flat since winning small-field Bath handicap for another stable a year ago; made fairly encouraging hurdle debut when keeping on for modest third at Plumpton (2m, good) last month but needs to build on that performance here and has since refused to race on the Flat.

runners_data.name: Pic N Mix
runners_data.note: Prominent racer but well held in recent Uttoxeter hurdle debut and lacks the class for this level.
runners_data.comment: Well held in both bumpers and on recent stable/hurdle debut
runners_data.spotlight: Well held in two bumpers for Michael Keady towards end of last year and also when reappearing in Uttoxeter maiden hurdle (2m good) for new stable this month.

runners_data.name: Trackman
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse winless in 23 Flat starts and 131 days absent makes him hard to recommend despite stamina appeal.
runners_data.comment: 0-23 on the Flat, having had several chances off basement marks; hurdle debut
runners_data.spotlight: 0-23 on the Flat, having had several chances off basement marks; should be fine stamina-wise over hurdles but makes very limited appeal.

races.paceDynamic: Edelak will take the field along from the front with Crackalackin, Garde My Guinness and Pic N Mix sitting prominent in the early stages. With only one confirmed front-runner, Edelak can dictate a sustainable gallop without serious pressure until the home turn. The pace will build gradually through the race as the prominently-raced horses engage from 3f out, before the hold-up horses Papillondelumiere, Backer Bilk, Versatile and Trackman attempt their late challenges. This measured early pace and gradual acceleration strongly favours hold-up horses who can finish with one sustained run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Edelak sets an honest but sustainable pace without serious early pressure
scenarios.body: The moderate early gallop allows the closers to get into perfect striking position turning for home, with their superior finishing kicks proving decisive in the final 2f. Hold-up specialists like Backer Bilk and Versatile can time their runs to perfection.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent racers prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the prominently-raced horses sustain their challenge from 3f out and kick clear
scenarios.body: Edelak's tactical speed combines with his hurdles experience to hold off late challengers, while Crackalackin's recent Fakenham third suggests he's ready to strike. The early leaders have enough left in the tank to resist the closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If no horse wants to make the running and the early pace becomes crawling
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where pure speed matters most, suiting horses with tactical pace regardless of their usual running style. Edelak's Flat speed background becomes crucial in a dash to the line.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Long-range winner emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one horse detaches from the field approaching the final flight with a sustained drive
scenarios.body: A patient ride on one of the better-credentialled horses pays dividends as they avoid the scramble and win with authority. Superior class tells in the closing stages despite the tactical disadvantage.

watchPoints.text: Edelak could set fractions too fast if other prominent horses pressure him early, which would set up the hold-up horses perfectly.
Garde My Guinness returning from 256 days off - watch market confidence and how sharp he looks in preliminaries.
Backer Bilk and Versatile both hold-up horses with similar profiles - watch which gets the better position turning for home.
Crackalackin needs Luke Scott to ride positively from the start to secure a good prominent position.
Track conditions firming up throughout the card - later runners may face quicker ground than advertised.

races.name: Tattersalls Online Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Cloudy Wednesday
runners_data.note: Front-running 10-year-old with course-and-distance win who should dictate terms from the front without early pressure
runners_data.comment: Won this in 2023; three of his four runs this year were very respectable; new headgear
runners_data.spotlight: Five chase wins, including 2023 edition of this race; pulled up at Fakenham two starts ago but his other three runs this year were very respectable; swaps usual cheekpieces for first-time blinkers; likely to give this a good shot from the front.

runners_data.name: Jack Doyen
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer in excellent recent form but needs the pace to be strong enough for his finishing kick to be effective
runners_data.comment: Ended last season with two 2m5f wins and ran well in defeat over 2m4f this month
runners_data.spotlight: Resurgent 10yo who ended last season with two 2m5f wins (good/good to soft) and posted another good effort when close second of 13 at Hexham (2m4f, good) this month; obvious contender.

runners_data.name: Kapamazov
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has been running too freely lately and needs to settle better to be competitive over this longer trip
runners_data.comment: Well beaten last time but ran quite well on stable debut and has slipped to a good mark
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten after racing too freely over 3m at Bangor last month and now 0-14 over fences but ran quite well when third on stable debut at Hereford (2m5f, good) in March and is suited by this track; sports refitted cheekpieces and has slipped to a good mark; dangerous to ignore.

runners_data.name: Pleasure Garden
runners_data.note: Prominent runner carrying bottom weight but struggles with stamina over this distance and hasn't won since 2023
runners_data.comment: Returned from layoff with two modest efforts towards end of last season; no win since 2023
runners_data.spotlight: Returned from layoff with two modest efforts towards end of last season (2m/2m1f) and remains without a win since 2023; yet to convince stamina-wise over this sort of trip; difficult to enthuse over.

runners_data.name: Chateau Du Lys
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who pulled up twice recently and needs significant improvement to be competitive despite his low weight
runners_data.comment: Only third best on merit when battling on for modest second last month; more needed here
runners_data.spotlight: Low-mileage 7yo; pulled up on consective appearances towards end of 2025 and was only third best on merit when battling on for modest second of six at Market Rasen (2m1f, good; first-time cheekpiecs) last month but at least that recent run gives him something to build on.

races.paceDynamic: Cloudy Wednesday will control this from the front with his confirmed leading style, setting a reasonable tempo over this 2m4f trip without early pressure from the small field. Jack Doyen and Chateau Du Lys as hold-up performers will track behind the prominent duo of Kapamazov and Pleasure Garden. The lack of pace pressure should create a tactical affair where stamina becomes crucial in the final half-mile. This race shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can avoid the scramble, while hold-up horses face the risk of the pace falling away too much for their closing kicks to be effective.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cloudy Wednesday Controls
scenarios.trigger: If the favourite gets an uncontested lead and dictates fractions
scenarios.body: Cloudy Wednesday can replicate his 2023 success here by controlling the tempo and having enough left for the finish. The lack of early pace pressure allows him to conserve energy for a sustained kick.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Kapamazov and Pleasure Garden track the leader closely and challenge approaching the final fence
scenarios.body: The two prominent runners can take advantage of their forward positions to strike when Cloudy Wednesday weakens. Their tactical positioning gives them first run on the hold-up horses behind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Success
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly pedestrian and the race develops into a sprint finish
scenarios.body: Jack Doyen's superior recent form and finishing kick could prove decisive if the race falls apart tactically. Chateau Du Lys might also benefit from a truly-run race despite his recent struggles.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Cloudy Wednesday goes too slow early and the field bunches up turning for home
scenarios.body: The entire field arrives together at the final fence creating a cavalry charge finish where class and current form become paramount. This chaotic finish could favour the most in-form runners regardless of style.

watchPoints.text: Cloudy Wednesday getting too soft a lead early - if uncontested he becomes very hard to peg back
Kapamazov settling properly behind the leaders - his recent free-running has compromised his chances
Jack Doyen's position turning into the straight - needs to be within striking distance for his kick to be effective
The pace through the first mile - if too slow the hold-up horses lose their tactical advantage
Pleasure Garden's stamina holding out - question marks remain about her ability to see out this trip strongly

races.name: Tattersalls Ireland May Hit & P2P Sale Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Ride Like A Girl
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner returning after 175 days and wind surgery, needs to prove fitness but unopposed for early lead
runners_data.comment: Only fourth when warm favourite for handicap debut but given wind op since; has potential
runners_data.spotlight: Managed only fourth of eight when warm favourite for handicap debut at Hereford (2m, good) in November and not seen since but had wind surgery in March and is now fitted with a tongue-tie; hood removed; probably still has potential.

runners_data.name: Callin Baton Rouge
runners_data.note: Patient hold-up type with strong finishing kick, suited by this race shape and excellent recent Stratford fourth
runners_data.comment: Didn't really have race run to suit when keeping-on fourth last month; 2lb lower here
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time hurdle winner who is usually ridden patiently; didn't really have race run to suit when keeping-on fourth at Stratford (2m, good) last month and is 2lb lower here; no surprise if she poses a threat.

runners_data.name: Alibey
runners_data.note: Races too freely which undermines finishing effort, but showed promise when second at Plumpton on handicap debut
runners_data.comment: Tends to race far too freely but went close on last month's handicap debut at Plumpton
runners_data.spotlight: Doesn't help herself by tending to race far too freely but belied 33-1 odds when close second on last month's handicap debut at Plumpton (2m, good) and has possibilities if Tabitha Worsley can keep a lid on her again here.

runners_data.name: Miracles Do Happen
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who benefits from tongue-tie after Taunton win, but needs to settle better than recent efforts
runners_data.comment: Scored at Taunton last month, her second handicap, and could have a lot more to offer
runners_data.spotlight: Safely held after racing too freely on handicap debut in March but displayed improvement to win at Taunton (2m, good; first-time tongue-tie) last month and could easily have more to offer; good chance.

runners_data.name: Eastern Shores
runners_data.note: Stays well and comes from rear, but hasn't convinced in three handicap starts and may lack pace for 2m
runners_data.comment: No threat to winner when second over C&D on handicap debut; two lesser efforts followed
runners_data.spotlight: Kept on from the rear for second over C&D (soft) on handicap debut in February but was no threat to the easy winner and two lesser efforts have followed; not written off just yet but needs to learn to settle better.

runners_data.name: Klervia
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with 5lb claimer, pulled up last time over longer trip but returning to more suitable distance
runners_data.comment: Given wind op after last month's poor run (2m5f); back in trip here; hard to predict
runners_data.spotlight: Bettered low-key stable debut when fourth of 13 in first-time cheekpieces at Exeter (2m5f, good) last month but was pulled up over that trip on next outing (given wind op soon afterwards) and it's hard to know what to expect from her back at about 2m.

runners_data.name: Adaay Dancing
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who looked out of sorts at Hereford, needs to recapture February Wincanton form
runners_data.comment: Looked out of sorts at Hereford last month and is now 0-7 over hurdles
runners_data.spotlight: Ran quite well when fourth of seven at Wincanton (1m7f, good to soft) in February, her second start for Max Comley, but looked out of sorts at Hereford last month and is now 0-7 over hurdles.

runners_data.name: Driving Miss d'Azy
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning after 193-day break under new training partnership, hard to assess current form

races.paceDynamic: Ride Like A Girl will set the pace from the front, with Alibey and Klervia likely to track her in prominent positions. The confirmed front-runner has no real pressure from other early pace types, allowing her to dictate a moderate tempo over this sharp 2m trip. The race will develop into a proper test from 3f out when the hold-up horses Callin Baton Rouge, Miracles Do Happen, and Eastern Shores try to mount their challenges. This sustainable pace scenario clearly favours the patient, hold-up types who can finish strongly when the early leaders tire.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is moderate and the hold-up brigade get clear runs
scenarios.body: Callin Baton Rouge, Miracles Do Happen, and Eastern Shores will have every chance to use their finishing kicks against tiring leaders. The patient tactics and strong closing sectionals will prove decisive over this sharp track.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Steal March
scenarios.trigger: If Ride Like A Girl gets away with soft fractions and kicks clear
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace pressure allows the leader to build an unassailable advantage, with Alibey potentially following her home. Hold-up horses left with too much to do in a slowly-run affair.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuine and both leaders and hold-up horses struggle
scenarios.body: Alibey and Klervia, positioned just behind the leader, get first run on the tiring pace-setter while avoiding the traffic problems. Their tactical positioning proves optimal in a messy finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If all the front-runners go too fast and burn out completely
scenarios.body: The race becomes a crawling affair until the final 2f, suiting only the most patient hold-up horses with tactical speed. Eastern Shores and Adaay Dancing benefit from being held up furthest.

watchPoints.text: Alibey could ruin her chances by racing too keen early and emptying her tank before the finish
Eastern Shores may struggle with the 2m trip being too sharp for her patient hold-up style
Ride Like A Girl's fitness levels after 175-day break and recent wind surgery will determine staying power
Miracles Do Happen needs to settle better than recent starts where she's raced too freely
Callin Baton Rouge getting a good tactical ride from the rear will be crucial to his winning chances

races.name: Tattersalls Online Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Thank You Ma'am
runners_data.note: Natural front runner with blinkers fitted but poor recent form suggests she may not handle early pace battle with Ballintubber Boy
runners_data.comment: Lost out only by a nose after making most of the running at Warwick last time
runners_data.spotlight: Returned from layoff with three below-par chase/hurdle runs in February/March but, having swapped cheekpieces for blinkers, fared much better on last two appearances; lost out only by a nose after making most of the running at Warwick (3m1f, good) last time; can make another bold bid.

runners_data.name: Ballintubber Boy
runners_data.note: Course and distance specialist returning from 210-day break but has winning record at this venue and proven stamina
runners_data.comment: Absent since two small-field seconds in October but is 3-3 over C&D; likely contender
runners_data.spotlight: Gained the last three of his seven hurdle wins over C&D (including 2024 edition of this race); absent since two small-field seconds in October (2m5f/2m7f) but there's a good chance he'll be primed for a big run on this return to Huntingdon.

runners_data.name: Kitty Foyle
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer whose recent Wincanton win may flatter but stays well and suits the likely strong pace
runners_data.comment: Wide-margin winner of three-runner race last month; value of that form open to question
runners_data.spotlight: Returned from break with wide-margin win in three-runner contest at Wincanton (3m, good) last month; the value of that form is open to question (leader crashed through rail and ran out in home straight) but she remains unexposed over this sort of trip and the handicapper has been pragmatic in raising her 4lb.

runners_data.name: Sunray Shadow
runners_data.note: Improved when stepped up to 2m7f last time and Harry Skelton booking suggests strong stable confidence
runners_data.comment: Looked suited by step up to 2m7f when clear second at Uttoxeter in March; shortlisted
runners_data.spotlight: Just 1-8 over hurdles but looked suited by the step up to 2m7f when clear second at Uttoxeter (good to soft) in March, where she travelled strongly for a long way; up in trip again here; must be considered.

runners_data.name: Tiger Orchid
runners_data.note: Consistent veteran who has been placed three times recently and handles this distance well
runners_data.comment: Runner-up all three starts for new stable towards end of last season; in the mix again
runners_data.spotlight: Without a win since summer 2024 and not getting any younger but runner-up three consecutive times (2m7f-3m1f; once over fences) for new stable towards end of last season; probably won't be far away.

runners_data.name: Alien Storm
runners_data.note: Better known as chaser now but stamina unproven at this extended hurdle trip despite recent Plumpton third
runners_data.comment: Ran well at Plumpton last month but has stamina to prove on first venture beyond 2m5f
runners_data.spotlight: Better known as a chaser now; gave good account when third of five over hurdles at regular haunt Plumpton (2m4f, good) last month but has stamina to prove on first venture beyond 2m5f.

runners_data.name: Gasmani
runners_data.note: Improving handicapper who won well at Taunton last month and handles the distance
runners_data.comment: Clear winner at Taunton last month and also ran well when second there a fortnight later
runners_data.spotlight: Displayed improvement to win by 5l at Taunton (3m, good) last month, his sixth hurdling start, and ran at least at well when close second over that C&D a fortnight later; respected in current mood.

runners_data.name: Billy Boi Blue
runners_data.note: Pulled up twice last season but previous form suggests ability to be competitive if handling the ground
runners_data.comment: Pulled up on last two outings but ran quite well until tiring on soft ground last time
runners_data.spotlight: Pulled up on consecutive appearances towards end of last season but seemed to run well until tiring on soft ground at Ayr last time; could be better suited by the less-testing conditions here; not ruled out.

races.paceDynamic: Thank You Ma'am and Ballintubber Boy are both confirmed front runners who will contest the early lead, ensuring an honest gallop from the start over this staying trip. With the majority of the field consisting of hold-up horses (Kitty Foyle, Sunray Shadow, Tiger Orchid, Alien Storm) and only two prominent runners (Gasmani, Billy Boi Blue), the pace will be solid but not frantic. The extended distance of 3m1f combined with good ground will allow the race to develop into a true stamina test. This pace dynamic strongly favours the hold-up horses who can settle behind the pace battle and use their stamina reserves in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the two front runners engage in a pace duel that takes its toll
scenarios.body: The early battle between Thank You Ma'am and Ballintubber Boy will set up the race perfectly for the patient hold-up horses to sweep past in the final half-mile. Sunray Shadow and Kitty Foyle have both shown strong finishing kicks when getting the trip, while Tiger Orchid's consistent recent placings suggest readiness to strike.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front runner survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leaders can dictate terms without serious early pressure
scenarios.body: Ballintubber Boy's course and distance winning record makes him the most likely to control the tempo and maintain his advantage, especially with his proven stamina over this extended trip. His class edge and proven ability at this venue could see him hold off the late challengers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent tracker strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners can position perfectly behind the pace battle
scenarios.body: Gasmani's recent improvement and Billy Boi Blue's freshness could see them track the leaders without getting involved in the early pace war. Their mid-race positioning allows them to launch telling challenges when the front runners begin to tire.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If both front runners fail to handle the early confrontation
scenarios.body: Thank You Ma'am's recent poor form and Ballintubber Boy's long absence could see both pace-setters capitulate, leaving the race to become a messy affair. This would particularly suit Tiger Orchid who has been running consistently well in similar handicaps.

watchPoints.text: Ballintubber Boy's 210-day absence could see him struggle for match fitness despite his course record
Thank You Ma'am's recent poor form makes her vulnerable if forced into early pace battle
Sunray Shadow's strong Uttoxeter second suggests she is ready to strike at this longer distance
Alien Storm's stamina is unproven over this extended hurdle trip having focused on chasing recently
Gasmani's recent improvement curve could continue with another step forward likely

races.name: Tattersalls Ireland May Hit & P2P Sale Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Lightning Flash
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning to hurdles after disappointing chase form, with Twiston-Davies team in moderate form but quick 13-day turnaround suggests confidence.
runners_data.comment: Looked laboured when remote third in two chases this spring; now back hurdling
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice over fences in the autumn (2m4f/2m) but looked laboured when remote third in two chases this spring; reverts to hurdling on a workable mark and with conditions suitable but needs this change of discipline to rekindle his enthusiam.

runners_data.name: Breezethroughlife
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits this pace scenario, trainer Neil King running at good strike-rate recently, and Fakenham third shows return to form over similar conditions.
runners_data.comment: Placed at Fakenham last month and didn't run badly in competitive race there two weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: Just 1-8 over hurdles but returned to form with pretty good third at Fakenham (2m7f, good) last month and didn't run badly in competitive 2m4f race there a fortnight ago; can make his presence felt.

runners_data.name: Ice Jet
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer faces tactical disadvantage but Skelton yard firing at 31% and comprehensive recent Bangor win shows he's well-handicapped when getting strong pace.
runners_data.comment: Won easily by 21l at Hereford last week; hard to beat under 7lb penalty here
runners_data.spotlight: Looked unlucky not to make winning handicap hurdle debut at Wetherby (2m, good to soft; made bad jumping error) in March but gained compensation with 21l win at Hereford (2m3f, good to firm) a week ago; ought to be hard to beat under 7lb penalty here.

runners_data.name: American Trio
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with finishing concerns, 42-day break since Exeter seller win, first-time visor worked last time but fade pattern remains worry.
runners_data.comment: Much-improved form when winning modest seller by 32l last month
runners_data.spotlight: Struggled on first two starts under rules but rewarded market support when winning modest Exeter seller (2m2f, good) by 32l in first-time visor last month; that form is tricky to evaluate but he remains unexposed.

races.paceDynamic: American Trio will lead from the start with no other confirmed front-runners to pressure him, setting a comfortable gallop over this extended trip. Lightning Flash and Breezethroughlife will settle prominently behind the leader, while Ice Jet drops in at the rear as a hold-up performer. American Trio's tendency to fade late means the pace will likely collapse in the final half-mile, creating a tactical finish. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track the pace and pounce when American Trio weakens, rather than hold-up horses facing a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If American Trio sets sustainable pace but fades as expected in final quarter-mile
scenarios.body: Lightning Flash or Breezethroughlife can strike from close range when the leader weakens, avoiding the need for a long sustained drive that hold-up horses require. The tactical finish suits horses already in contention turning for home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Lasts Home
scenarios.trigger: If American Trio's 42-day break has improved his stamina and he resists challengers better than form suggests
scenarios.body: The uncontested lead and good ground conditions allow him to maintain his advantage despite previous finishing concerns. His comprehensive Exeter win suggests potential improvement in the headgear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely strong with prominent horses pushing American Trio along earlier than expected
scenarios.body: Ice Jet benefits from a truly-run race where his closing kick becomes decisive in a stamina test. His Skelton yard form and recent Bangor success show he can quicken off a strong pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If American Trio stops quickly before the final turn, creating a messy tactical affair
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the second-last hurdle where any horse can win from any position. This chaotic scenario levels the playing field but favours the most reliable jumpers.

watchPoints.text: American Trio's jumping under pressure - made errors when challenged in previous starts and any mistake when tiring could bring down tracking horses
Lightning Flash's settling ability early - if he races keenly behind American Trio, he'll compromise his prominent tactics and play into Ice Jet's hands
Ice Jet's position turning in - needs to be within striking distance of leaders when American Trio weakens or he'll face impossible task
Breezethroughlife's stamina reserves at this trip - stepping up from 2m4f recent runs to 2m4½f on faster ground than ideal
American Trio's jumping rhythm in first two furlongs - if he's not fluent early, the prominent horses will crowd him and force stronger pace

races.name: Tattersalls Online Novices' Hunters' Chase

runners_data.name: Kandor
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist returning after 369 days off which is a significant concern despite his proven class
runners_data.comment: Won small-field open point last month and probably has a big role to play in this
runners_data.spotlight: Fair handicapper when trained by Lucinda Russell and 2-6 in points for current stable, the latter win gained in three-runner mixed open at Edgcote (3m, good) last month; probably has a big role to play in this.

runners_data.name: O'Hallorans Castle
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose recent form figures flatter modest actual performances and tends to fade in the finish
runners_data.comment: This year's pointing form is not as inspiring as his recent form-figures might suggest
runners_data.spotlight: Won two 3m points last year but this year's pointing form is not as inspiring as his recent form-figures might suggest, and others in this line-up look stronger.

runners_data.name: Sambezi
runners_data.note: Older prominent runner showing return to form in points but may lack the class for this level
runners_data.comment: Fair hurdler in his prime; back in good form in points this spring; one to consider
runners_data.spotlight: Fair hurdler in his prime; returned to form when dead-heating with good hunter chaser in two-runner point in March and backed up that performance with very respectable third in Garthorpe open (3m, good; tongue-tie/cheekpieces refitted) last month; one to consider.

runners_data.name: Whats The Solution
runners_data.note: Natural front runner with recent good form but struggled badly at higher level in Aintree Foxhunters
runners_data.comment: Six point wins, the latest an open this year; this is much easier than latest rules run
runners_data.spotlight: 6-22 in points, the latest win gained in Friars Haugh open (2m4f, good to soft) in March; predictably struggled in Aintree Foxhunters' last month and ran out in early stages of a subsequent point but has good claims if all goes to plan here.

runners_data.name: On Lovers Walk
runners_data.note: Prominent runner coming off a tactical win at Fakenham just 18 days ago with good course form
runners_data.comment: Found 2m too sharp last month; has claims if judged on 3m Fakenham win in April
runners_data.spotlight: Led close home to win tactical hunter chase at Fakenham (3m, good) last month; found things happening too quickly and jumped badly right throughout when remote last of three at Warwick (2m, good) 18 days ago but moves back up in trip here and the switch to a right-handed track ought to suit.

runners_data.name: J'envoievalserenki
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who fades in finish but won his latest point in first-time visor which he retains
runners_data.comment: 2-7 in points for this stable since the autumn; top amateur James King booked again
runners_data.spotlight: 2-7 in points for current stable since this autumn, the latter win gained in four-runner conditions race at Mollington (3m, good to firm; first-time visor; odds-on favourite fell) this month; has more on his plate here but top amateur James King is booked again.

runners_data.name: Surprise Attack
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with solid recent form including close second at Witton Castle just two weeks ago
runners_data.comment: 6-21 in points; close second at Witton Castle this month; ought to be competitive here
runners_data.spotlight: 6-21 in points; yet to win this year but went down fighting when close second at Witton Castle (3m, good) a fortnight ago and ought to be competitive in this.

races.paceDynamic: Whats The Solution will dictate proceedings from the front with his proven front-running style, likely getting an uncontested lead in this small field. The prominent runners O'Hallorans Castle, Sambezi and On Lovers Walk will track him but none are aggressive enough to create early pressure. This sets up a tactical affair where the pace will be steady early before quickening from the home turn. The lack of early pace pressure clearly favours the hold-up horses Kandor, J'envoievalserenki and Surprise Attack who can use their finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Profit
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace stays moderate as expected with Whats The Solution unchallenged
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the home turn where late runners can unleash their finishing speed. Kandor and Surprise Attack are perfectly positioned to capitalize on this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If On Lovers Walk or Sambezi apply more early pressure than anticipated
scenarios.body: The increased gallop stretches the field and prevents the hold-up horses from getting into contention. On Lovers Walk's recent Fakenham win shows he can handle a stronger pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Whats The Solution maintains his recent good form and kicks clear turning in
scenarios.body: His class advantage tells as he builds an unassailable lead before the closers can respond. The modest opposition fails to mount a serious challenge in the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes crawling with no one willing to challenge Whats The Solution
scenarios.body: The race turns into a messy sprint where stamina becomes irrelevant and any horse can win. Form goes out the window in a blanket finish decided by jumping errors.

watchPoints.text: Whats The Solution could get an easy lead and prove hard to peg back if his Aintree disappointment was just a class issue
Kandor's 369-day absence is huge for a hold-up horse who needs to be sharp to deliver his finishing kick
On Lovers Walk carries 4lbs extra but has winning momentum from his recent Fakenham success
Watch for early market moves on J'envoievalserenki as his first-time visor worked well last time
The good to firm ground could expose any stamina doubts in this extended trip for the lesser-exposed runners
